answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to one slow, non-transferable proof of useful work that cannot be cloned cheaply. Before an agent can trade, it must finish a unique, epoch-seeded task and earn peer attestations over time, so reputation accrues only to a lived history. A mesa of fresh clones looks broad from above but has no depth: each copy must pay the same time cost again, while a haven of trust forms only around proven agents. Like onyx, a reputation carved once cannot be mass-copied, so splitting into thousands dilutes influence instead of multiplying it.
